# How the decisionsjs parser decides

<!-- generated by `node src/cli.ts <grammar.ts> --decisions` from the portable plan (src/ir/parser-ir.ts) of `decisionsjs.ts`; do not edit by hand. -->

Every choice point of the grammar and how the generated parser (the portable plan every target prints) decides it: by one token, by two tokens, by attempt (an ordered choice tries its branches in order; a repetition without a FIRST guard tries its body), or by longest match in a candidate frame; and whether it takes a mark that a failure restores. Then the findings a grammar author should act on, each with its witness and a suggested action. How it is derived: src/ir/decision-report.ts.

## Findings

### Dead alternatives

It always matches exactly one token, and at every token it admits a candidate declared before it is surely tried and matches at least that token: the earlier one wins the tie, so this one never wins. For the root grammars `node test/decision-report.ts --dead` removes each from the grammar and requires that no tree on the corpora changes.

| list | dead alternative | taken by | at | witness | action |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Expr NUD | true_ (#2) | ident (#0) | `true` | `true` as Expr | remove the arm, or declare it before `ident` / guard `ident`: `ident`, declared before it, takes every input it could match |

### Ties decided by declaration order

Two candidates of one list can both match exactly one token at these tokens, to the same end; the one declared first wins there. Where the later one is meant to win, the grammar must say so (reorder, or refuse the token in the earlier one). The witness is that token parsed as the rule. This page has the static ties only: the ties a real input meets (how often, and where) come from running the parser over inputs: `node test/decision-report.ts --observe <grammar.ts> <input files>`.

| list | wins (declared first) | loses | one token | witness | action |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| Expr NUD | ident (#0) | this_ (#3) | `this` | `this` as Expr | reorder, or guard `ident`: the tie of ident and this_ on `this` is resolved only by declaration order (ident wins) |

### Alternatives no token reaches

None.

## Choice points

Per rule: its candidate lists (every key and what decides it), then the inline choices and repetitions that are not decided by one token without a mark (the others are counted).

### Expr

- Expr NUD (5 NUD arms):
  - `(`: one token: committed to paren (#4) (takes a mark: it can fail after `'('`)
  - <Ident>: one token: committed to ident (#0)
  - <Number>: one token: committed to number (#1)
  - punctuation: no candidate, the list fails
  - longest match: a candidate frame (a mark per new best) at `this`, `true`, over ident (#0), true_ (#2), this_ (#3)
- Expr NUD / this_: `opt('.' Ident)`: one token; takes a mark: it can fail after `'.'`
